lines.japanese:
「君の仕事に手を出すのは出しゃばりだと思うが。
　なあ、まずはその紙切れを全部拾おうぜ」
lines.english:
“I don't mean to take over your work,
but… Let's pick up all those bits of paper first.”

lines.japanese:
出来れば朔屋も、寝台を直すふりしてさぼりを決めこみたい。水夫長とていちいち監視に来るほど暇でもなかろう。だいたいこんな狭い部屋の掃除くらい一人で充分だ、それにこのクロというのは、信天翁号の雑用か何かだろうし、だったらこれも彼女の仕事、手を出してしまうのも領分違い───
　───に、割りきれず、寝台からのそのそ埃の中に這い出して、紙切れを拾い始めてしまうあたり、怠け者にも徹し切れぬこの青年の中途半端さがある。粉っぽくなってしまった室内の空気、なるたけ吸わないようにと身を屈める朔屋の脇でクロは、硬直していた。怪訝に見上げれば、
lines.english:
Sakuya, for his part, would have preferred to pretend to straighten the berth and settle in for a good spell of shirking. Surely even the boatswain had better things to do than keep coming around to check on him. Cleaning a little room this cramped was a one-person job to begin with; besides, this Kuro girl must be some sort of odd-job hand aboard the Albatross, which made it her work, and his pitching in a trespass upon another’s province—
—except he could not quite bring himself to leave it at that. He lumbered out of the berth and into the dust and began gathering up scraps of paper: there, in a nutshell, was this young man’s half-measured nature, incapable even of making a thoroughgoing idler of himself. As he stooped, trying to inhale as little as possible of the air gone powdery with dust, Kuro stood rigid beside him. Puzzled, he looked up at her.

lines.japanese: 「すいません、です。あの、ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. Um… sorry.”
“…? What for?”

lines.japanese:
「クロはぐずで、ぶきっちょな、クロだから。
　朔屋さんに、やらせちゃう……」
lines.english:
“Kuro's so slow, and clumsy…
You end up doing it, Mr. Sakuya…”

lines.japanese: ……肩を細く強張らせて、俯き加減なのが、今にも不器用を叱られ頭を殴られるのを待ち構えているよう。戦慄かせる目元に、逃げ出したいのを必死に抑えつける内心がありありと、これには朔屋もまずは暗澹となった。次に尾籠にも頭をもたげてきたのは加虐心だったというなんともはや、この少女をからかい混じりにこづき回したらどうなるのかと心がついつい動きそうになる。
lines.japaneseRuby: ……肩を細く強張らせて、[R俯^うつむ]き加減なのが、今にも不器用を叱られ頭を殴られるのを待ち構えているよう。[R戦慄^わなな]かせる目元に、逃げ出したいのを必死に抑えつける内心がありありと、これには朔屋もまずは[R暗澹^あんたん]となった。次に[R尾籠^びろう]にも頭をもたげてきたのは加虐心だったというなんともはや、この少女をからかい混じりにこづき回したらどうなるのかと心がついつい動きそうになる。
lines.english: Shoulders drawn tight, head slightly bowed, she looked as though she were bracing herself to be scolded for her clumsiness and struck on the head at any moment. Her trembling eyes showed how hard she was fighting not to bolt, and at that sight Sakuya's mood first turned gloomy. Then, disgracefully, cruelty began to stir in him. What a creature he was: he found himself wondering what would happen if he teased this girl and knocked her about.

lines.japanese: 泣くのか、あのへつらうような笑みで誤魔化すのか、それとももっと別の表情を見せてくれるのか。そんな彼女の、埃まみれの白髪を、払ってやるふりして軽く引っぱったりなどしてやるのもいいかも知れない。荒廃した船室の中に白子の哀れな少女を置くと、それはそれで痛々しいなりの興趣があって、ついつい朔屋の妄想いかがわしくもそそられる。
lines.english: Would she cry? Hide it behind that fawning smile? Or show him some other face altogether? Perhaps he might pretend to brush the dust from her white hair and give it a little tug. Put one pitiful albino girl in a ruined cabin and the picture acquired its own wretched fascination—quite enough to set Sakuya's disreputable imagination pleasantly astir.

lines.japanese: なんだったら、クロのレギンスの埃を叩き落とす、モノのはずみで引きずり降ろしてやるのもいい。晒されたような白の、痩せた腿[もも]や脚には埃汚れも目立つだろうそれが面白い、履き直すこと許してやらなかったら、クロは逆らえず、下半身丸出しのまま埃と苦戦するのだろう。そこにあるのは性的好奇心などいう生々しい情欲などでなく、悪童が女児のスカートをまくって馬鹿笑いするのと同じ質の幼稚気だが、いずれにしても嘆かわしい。さあ髪を引っぱるかレギンスを降ろすかと、悪戯心のままに朔屋の手は立ち尽くしたクロへと伸びて、彼の目は人としてあるまじきのさもしい光に揺らぎ、揺らいで、ふっとまたもとの小心な朔屋に戻って、手を伸ばしたのは紙切れにと。
lines.english: For that matter, he might brush the dust from Kuro's leggings and yank them down in the process. The dirt would show nicely on those thin, exposed legs, white as though bleached; that would be amusing. If he then refused to let her pull them back up, Kuro would be unable to defy him and would have to keep fighting the dust with her lower half bare. This was not sexual curiosity, nothing so raw as lust, but the same childish impulse that makes a brat flip up a girl's skirt and howl with laughter—deplorable all the same. Hair or leggings, then? Carried by the mischief, Sakuya reached toward the motionless Kuro, his eyes wavering with a mean little light unworthy of any human being. Then the light vanished. He was his usual timid self again, and his hand reached instead for a scrap of paper.

lines.japanese:
「……いいから。二人でやるのが早いから。
　俺はこっちのほう拾うから、君ゃあっちな」
lines.english:
“…Never mind. It'll be quicker with two of us.
I'll pick up this side. You do over there.”

lines.japanese: 「あい」
lines.english: “'Kay.”

lines.japanese: こっくり頷[うなず]いた、クロの顔には感謝の感激朔屋の気恥ずかしいほどにありありと、どうやら少女は青年の寸前の目の色を見ずに済んだらしい。あるいは見ていてなお気づかないくらいに鈍感だったのかもしれないが、ともかく二人は動き出して、片づけはようやくまともに進む。朔屋がもっと早くに、クロが働きだした辺りで声をかけていたなら、七割方は終わっていたであろう頃合いで。
lines.english:
She nodded. Her gratitude shone so plainly on her face that he felt embarrassed. Apparently she had missed the look in his eyes a moment earlier. Or perhaps she had seen it and was too dull to recognize it. In any case, they began moving, and the cleaning finally made proper progress.
Had he spoken up sooner, when Kuro first started work, they would probably have been seventy percent finished by now.

lines.japanese: ……と、言えば後はいかにもてきぱきと進んだように聞こえる。実体はさに非ずして、クロは何枚か紙を拾い上げたところで手から取り零し、またやり直しする事になり、それを二回ばかり繰り返した。ようやくしっかり握る事を覚えた辺りで、後方不注意で朔屋の脚にけつまずき、埃の床に頭からのめって思いきり綿ごみ吸いこみ、激しくむせかえっては掃除を中断させた。しまいには朔屋も苛立ち始め、今度不始末をしでかしたら部屋から叩き出そうと決意した早々に、小さな悲鳴がクロから。
lines.english: …Put that way, it sounds as though matters proceeded with exemplary dispatch thereafter. The reality was otherwise. Kuro would pick up several sheets only to drop them from her hand and have to begin again, and this she repeated twice. Just as she finally learned to keep a firm grip on them, she neglected what lay behind her, tripped over Sakuya’s leg, pitched headfirst into the dusty floor, inhaled a great wad of lint, and brought the cleaning to a halt with a violent fit of coughing. By the end even Sakuya’s patience had begun to fray. He had only just resolved to throw her out of the room if she bungled one more thing when a little shriek came from Kuro.

lines.japanese:
憤然と向き直れば、ぎゅっと、片手の人差し指をきつく握りしめておろおろと、指先から彼女の目の色と同じ赤い雫が膨らんで、張り詰めてから滴ってたらり、とうとうたらり、床の埃に落ちていく。
　紙切れの端で指先を切ったと思しく、クロにしてみれば血止めのつもりで指の根元を押さえているのだろうが、それでは絞り出しているだけ。薔薇を摘[つ]む令嬢が棘に傷して、薔薇園の地に少女の生命の雫を吸わせている情景なら、唯美主義者が喜んで画にも描く詩文にも語ろう。しかし痩せっぽちのクロが、適当に掃き寄せられた埃の上に赤いのを零してじくじく空しく吸わせていくとあっては痛さ間抜けさの方が先に立ち、朔屋は気勢を削がれて、ポケットから鼻紙を引っぱり出した。くしゃくしゃによれてはいたが幸い未使用で、クロの指先に宛う。
lines.english:
He wheeled around indignantly. Kuro stood there in a panic, clutching one forefinger. At its tip a bead of red—the color of her eyes—swelled, drew taut, and fell; then another dropped into the dust.
She had apparently cut herself on the edge of a scrap of paper. She must have thought gripping the base of the finger would stop the bleeding, but she was only squeezing more out. A young lady pricked by a thorn as she plucked a rose, letting drops of her life soak into the rose garden: an aesthete might delight in painting such a scene or celebrating it in verse. But scrawny Kuro bleeding into a carelessly swept heap of dust looked painful and foolish before it looked beautiful. Sakuya's indignation deserted him. He pulled a tissue from his pocket. It was crumpled but, fortunately, unused, and he pressed it to her fingertip.

lines.japanese: 「なにやってんだかなぁ……。ほら、そうやって血が止まるまで押さえてな。紙の切り傷は、刃物より痛いが我慢しろよ？」
lines.english: “What are you doing…? Here. Hold it like that until the blood stops. A paper cut hurts more than a knife cut, but you'll have to bear it.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あい……。
　あの、ちり紙、
　あとで洗って返す……します」
lines.english:
“O-Okay… Um, the tissue…
I'll wash it and give it…
give it back later.”

lines.japanese:
「んなモン洗ったら溶けちまうわ。
　いいから、ちょっと座ってなよ。
　後は俺がやるから」
lines.english:
“Wash it and it'll fall apart.
Just sit down a bit.
I'll do the rest.”

lines.japanese:
クロには手出しさせない方がまだましだとやっと気づくあたり、朔屋も相当に無能で、実際室内はクロが入る前より散らかっていた。が、黙々と進めてみれば、元は大して私物もなかった船室である。片づけも埃払いも本気で手を着けてみればあっけなく、それでもやはり、終わった頃には青年の額や首筋には汗。
　拭い拭いしながら背を伸ばし凝りをほぐしていると、寝台ではクロがえへえへと手を打っていた。
lines.english:
Only now did he realize that keeping Kuro out of the work was better. That said little for his own competence. The room was, in fact, messier than before she entered.
Still, it had contained few possessions to begin with. Once he quietly set to work in earnest, the tidying and dusting were soon done. By the end, nonetheless, sweat stood on his forehead and neck.
He wiped it away, straightened his back, and stretched the stiffness out. On the berth, Kuro was giggling and clapping.

lines.japanese:
「凄い、凄い、朔屋さん。
　これだったら、クロがしなかった方が、
　早いかったみたい。
　最初から朔屋さん、してれば、よかったね」
lines.english:
“Amazing! Amazing, Mr. Sakuya!
It looks like…
it would've been quicker if Kuro hadn't helped.
You should've done it right from the start.”

lines.japanese: 真実そうかも知れないといえ、それを本人が言ってしまってはおしまいだろうと、朔屋の片頬が引きつる。無言で寝台の端に腰かけるクロの前に立ち、
lines.english: It might be true, but surely she should not be the one to say it. His cheek twitched. Without a word, he stood before Kuro, seated on the edge of the berth.

lines.japanese:
「な、なにぃ……？
　なんか、怒って……る、ね？」
lines.english:
“Wh-What…?
You're sort of… angry, aren't you?”
“—Eeeeek!—”

lines.japanese: 朔屋は遂に拳を固め、いややっぱり殴ってしまうのは一線を越えてしまう気がして踏み切れず、代わりに朔屋はクロをベッドに押し倒し、その脚をぐいと抱えこみ───蹠をくすぐり責めにしたという。
lines.japaneseRuby: 朔屋は遂に拳を固め、いややっぱり殴ってしまうのは一線を越えてしまう気がして踏み切れず、代わりに朔屋はクロをベッドに押し倒し、その脚をぐいと抱えこみ───[R蹠^あしうら]をくすぐり責めにしたという。
lines.english: At last Sakuya clenched his fist. No—actually hitting her still seemed a line he could not cross. Instead, he pushed her back onto the bed, caught her legs, and subjected the soles of her feet to a merciless tickling.

lines.japanese:
「あ、は、あははははははっ、
　あは、かはっ、苦し……いひひひひひっ、
　止め……えへへへへっ、かはっ、もっ、
　か、かんにん……ひひひ、ひぃ～～っっ」
lines.english:
“Ah, ha, ahahahahaha!
Aha, kah, can't brea—heeheeheehee!
Sto—ehehehehe!
Kh, no mo—m-mercy… heehee, heeeeee!”

lines.japanese: クロは呼吸困難寸前になるまで笑い狂って、責めが止んだ頃には息も絶え絶え、青年を見つめる真っ赤な目には、怨みがましいような、殴りはしなかった事を不思議と思っているようなどっちつかずの色が浮いたのだった。
lines.english: Kuro laughed until she was almost unable to breathe. When the torment stopped, she lay gasping. The look in the scarlet eyes turned on him was ambiguous: something like resentment, something like wonder that he had not hit her.
